translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to salt transport commissioner of the Lianghuai region but remained in Hubei to manage the grain bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng (1856) he was transferred to salt transport commissioner of the Lianghuai region but remained in Hubei to run the grain supply bureau.

sentences.zh: 游勇煽饑民為亂，蔓延荊、襄、鄖、宜四郡，遵殿固守，待援兵至，大破之。

translations.literal: Roving braves incited hungry people to rebellion, which spread through the four prefectures of Jing, Xiang, Yun, and Yi; Zundian held firm until relief troops arrived and routed them thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Roving soldiers incited hungry civilians to revolt across the Jing, Xiang, Yun, and Yi prefectures; Zundian held his ground until reinforcements arrived and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，武漢克復，遵殿力固上游。

translations.literal: That autumn Wuhan was recovered, and Zundian worked strenuously to secure the upper reaches.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when Wuhan was recovered, he labored to secure the upper Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 以盜賊起於飢寒，勸置義倉七十餘所，以稅餘銀修老龍堤捍水患，就遷湖北按察使。

translations.literal: Believing that banditry arose from hunger and cold, he urged the establishment of more than seventy charity granaries and used surplus tax silver to repair the Laolong embankment against flooding, and was thereupon promoted to provincial judicial commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that banditry sprang from hunger and cold, he urged the establishment of more than seventy charity granaries and devoted surplus tax revenue to repairing the Laolong embankment against floods; he was then promoted to provincial judicial commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng (1858) he was promoted to provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 時胡林翼為巡撫，百廢具舉，重遵殿清德，吏事悉倚之。

translations.literal: At that time Hu Linyi was governor; he restored every neglected affair and valued Zundian's integrity, relying on him entirely for administrative business.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi was then governor of the province, reviving every neglected institution; he prized Zundian's integrity and entrusted him with virtually all administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢福建巡撫，未之任，調浙江。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to governor of Fujian but did not take up the post and was transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xianfeng (1859) he was promoted to governor of Fujian but before taking office was transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 自賊踞江寧，皖南軍事餉事悉隸浙江。

translations.literal: Since the rebels held Jiangning, military and supply affairs in southern Anhui all fell under Zhejiang's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels held Nanjing, military operations and supplies for southern Anhui all fell under Zhejiang's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 屯兵寧國，恃為屏蔽。

translations.literal: Troops were encamped at Ningguo and relied upon as a protective screen.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops were stationed at Ningguo and counted on as a shield for the province.

sentences.zh: 及胡興仁為巡撫，不欲餉鄰軍，又劾統將鄭魁士他調去，賊窺浙益急。

translations.literal: When Hu Xingren became governor he was unwilling to supply neighboring armies and also impeached the commanding general Zheng Kuishi for transfer elsewhere; the rebels' probing of Zhejiang grew more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Xingren became governor he refused to provision neighboring armies and impeached the commanding general Zheng Kuishi for transfer elsewhere, and rebel probes against Zhejiang grew steadily more threatening.

sentences.zh: 遵殿到官，痛吏習浮競，乃嚴舉劾，察營伍，或不便其所為，多毀之。

translations.literal: When Zundian took office he detested officials' habit of empty rivalry, enforced strict impeachments, and inspected the camps; those inconvenienced by his conduct largely slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Zundian detested the officials' habit of empty rivalry; he enforced strict impeachments and inspected the camps, and those who found his conduct inconvenient spread slander against him.

sentences.zh: 省垣獨總兵李定太軍六千人，知不足恃，與胡林翼商調楚軍，倉猝難應。

translations.literal: The provincial capital had only the six thousand troops of Brigadier-general Li Dingtai; knowing this insufficient, he consulted Hu Linyi on transferring Chu army units, but in the haste no response could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial capital had only Brigadier-general Li Dingtai's six thousand men, which he knew were insufficient; he consulted Hu Linyi about transferring Hunan troops, but in the emergency no help could arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 賊已由寧國竄入浙境。

translations.literal: The rebels had already slipped from Ningguo into Zhejiang territory.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had already broken out of Ningguo into Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 遣李定太出防湖州，而廣德已陷。

translations.literal: He sent Li Dingtai out to defend Huzhou, but Guangde had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Li Dingtai to defend Huzhou, but Guangde had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，賊由獨松關逼杭州，湖南遣蕭翰慶、李元度兩軍來援，翰慶戰死，元度道阻不得前。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year rebels pressed Hangzhou through Dusong Pass; Hunan sent the two armies of Xiao Hanqing and Li Yuandu to relieve it; Hanqing died in battle and Yuandu was blocked on the road and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year of Xianfeng (1860), rebels pressed Hangzhou through Dusong Pass; Hunan dispatched the armies of Xiao Hanqing and Li Yuandu to relieve the city; Hanqing was killed in battle and Yuandu was blocked on the road and could not advance.

sentences.zh: 賊壁城南山上，下臨城中。

translations.literal: The rebels fortified on the southern mountain outside the city and looked down upon the town below.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fortified on the hills south of the city and looked down on the streets below.

sentences.zh: 乞師江南，未至，兵少，實不能戰。

translations.literal: He begged troops from Jiangnan, but they did not arrive; his forces were few and he truly could not fight.
translations.idiomatic: He begged for troops from Jiangnan, but they did not arrive; his forces were too few to offer a real fight.

sentences.zh: 浙西初經寇亂，人不知兵，議戰議守，紛紜不定。

translations.literal: Western Zhejiang had only lately suffered rebel ravages; the people knew nothing of war, and debate over fighting versus holding the city was chaotic and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhejiang had only lately been ravaged by rebels; civilians knew nothing of war, and debate over whether to fight or hold the walls raged without resolution.

sentences.zh: 會久雨，遵殿徒步泥淖中，守浹旬，城陷，仰藥死，妻女同殉，詔予優恤。

translations.literal: As the rains persisted long, Zundian walked on foot through the mud defending for ten days; the city fell, he took poison and died, his wife and daughters martyred together, and an edict granted generous condolence.
translations.idiomatic: As the rains dragged on, Zundian walked barefoot through the mud and held the city for ten days; when it fell he took poison and died, his wife and daughters dying with him, and the court granted generous posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 尋以御史高延祜奏劾遵殿不能禦賊，罷其卹典。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the censor Gao Yanhu memorialized impeaching Zundian for failing to repel the rebels, and his condolence honors were revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Censor Gao Yanhu memorialized that Zundian had failed to repel the rebels, and his posthumous honors were revoked.

sentences.zh: 遵殿任外吏二十年，廉介絕俗，家僅土屋數椽，胡林翼集賻，乃克歸喪。

translations.literal: Zundian served as a local official for twenty years, his integrity beyond the vulgar; his home had only a few mud-walled rooms, and only when Hu Linyi collected funeral contributions could the coffin be returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zundian had served as a local official for twenty years with an integrity beyond the common run; his household owned only a few mud-walled rooms, and only when Hu Linyi raised funeral contributions could his coffin be brought home.

sentences.zh: 同治初，詔允曾國籓之請，念其歷官有聲，到浙未久，追贈右都御史，予騎都尉世職，諡壯節。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi an edict approved Zeng Guofan's request, remembering his distinguished service in office though his stay in Zhejiang had been brief; he was posthumously promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, granted the hereditary office of Rider Captain, and given the posthumous name Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign (1862), the court granted Zeng Guofan's request, recalling his distinguished record though his tenure in Zhejiang had been brief; he was posthumously promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, granted the hereditary office of Rider Captain, and given the posthumous name Zhuangjie (Stalwart Integrity).

sentences.zh: 城陷時，署布政使王友端、署按察使繆梓、杭嘉湖道葉堃、寧紹台道仲孫懋、署杭州知府馬昂霄、署仁和知縣李福謙同殉節。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the acting provincial treasurer Wang Youduan, acting provincial judicial commissioner Mou Zi, Hang-Jia-Hu circuit intendant Ye Kun, Ning-Shao-Tai circuit intendant Zhongsun Mao, acting Hangzhou prefect Ma Angxiao, and acting Renhe magistrate Li Fuqian all died martyrs together.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Acting Provincial Treasurer Wang Youduan, Acting Provincial Judicial Commissioner Mou Zi, Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit Intendant Ye Kun, Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit Intendant Zhongsun Mao, Acting Hangzhou Prefect Ma Angxiao, and Acting Renhe Magistrate Li Fuqian all died in its defense.

sentences.zh: 友端，安徽婺源人。

translations.literal: Youduan was a native of Wuyuan in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Youduan was a native of Wuyuan in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七進士，授戶部主事，遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of the Daoguang reign (1847), was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 出為浙江糧道，署布政使。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as grain intendant of Zhejiang and acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grain intendant of Zhejiang and served concurrently as acting provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 當粵匪之窺浙也，言於遵殿曰：「皖邊軍弱，湖州空虛，請速備廣德。」

translations.literal: When Cantonese rebels were probing Zhejiang he said to Zundian: "The troops on the Anhui border are weak and Huzhou stands empty; please quickly prepare Guangde."
translations.idiomatic: When Cantonese rebels threatened Zhejiang he told Zundian, "The troops on the Anhui border are weak and Huzhou lies exposed; prepare Guangde at once."

sentences.zh: 遵殿至事急始遣軍，已無及。

translations.literal: Zundian only dispatched troops when matters grew urgent, and it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: Zundian sent troops only when the crisis was upon him, and it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 賊遂長驅至城下，友端復請列塹湧金、清波兩門為犄角，亦不用其言。

translations.literal: The rebels then drove straight to the foot of the city walls; Youduan again requested trenches at the Yongjin and Qingbo gates as pincer positions, but again his words were not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then drove straight to the walls; Youduan again urged entrenchments at the Yongjin and Qingbo gates as mutual supports, but again his advice went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 賊穴道攻城，友端懸金三千募死士縋擊，遇雨，火器不燃而敗。

translations.literal: The rebels tunneled to assault the city; Youduan offered three thousand taels of gold to recruit desperados lowered by rope to strike them, but rain came, the firearms would not ignite, and they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tunneled under the walls; Youduan offered three thousand taels of gold to recruit desperados to be lowered by rope for a sortie, but rain fell, their firearms failed to ignite, and the attack was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 臨死，自書「浙江布政使王友端」八字於衿上，予騎都尉世職，諡貞介。

translations.literal: Before death he himself wrote the eight characters "Zhejiang Provincial Treasurer Wang Youduan" on his collar; he was granted the hereditary office of Rider Captain and given the posthumous name Zhenjie.
translations.idiomatic: Before he died he wrote on his collar the eight characters "Zhejiang Provincial Treasurer Wang Youduan"; he was granted the hereditary office of Rider Captain and given the posthumous name Zhenjie (Upright and Incorruptible).

sentences.zh: 梓，江蘇溧陽人。

translations.literal: Zi was a native of Liyang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Zi was a native of Liyang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光八年舉人，大挑知縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination and through the great selection was appointed magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the eighth year of the Daoguang reign (1828) and through the great selection was appointed magistrate.

sentences.zh: 歷署仙居、石門、奉化諸縣。

translations.literal: He successively acted as magistrate of Xianju, Shimen, Fenghua, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as acting magistrate of Xianju, Shimen, Fenghua, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 罣誤去官。

translations.literal: Implicated in an error, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Caught up in an official error, he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 值清查倉庫、水災籌賑，奉檄佐理，皆得其力。

translations.literal: During the granary inspection and flood-relief planning he received orders to assist and in every case gained their strength.
translations.idiomatic: During the granary inspection and flood-relief campaigns he was ordered to assist and proved indispensable in both.

sentences.zh: 準捐輸复官，晉同知。

translations.literal: Permitted to restore his office by contribution, he was promoted to sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Permitted to restore his office through a contribution, he was promoted to sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，河決阻漕，獻策行海運，即以任之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng the Yellow River burst its banks and blocked the grain transport route; he proposed sea transport and was immediately assigned to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng (1852), when a breach of the Yellow River blocked the grain route, he proposed shifting transport to the sea and was immediately put in charge.

sentences.zh: 蕆事，擢知府。

translations.literal: When the task was completed he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When the task was completed he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 上海為賊陷，率兵助剿；

translations.literal: When Shanghai fell to the rebels he led troops to assist in suppression;
translations.idiomatic: When Shanghai fell to the rebels he led troops to assist in the suppression;

sentences.zh: 复創議疏濬劉河海口以通漕運。

translations.literal: He also pioneered a proposal to dredge the mouth of the Liu River to open the grain transport route.
translations.idiomatic: He also pioneered a proposal to dredge the mouth of the Liu River to restore the grain transport route.

sentences.zh: 歷寧波、杭州知府，署杭嘉湖道，兼鹽運使。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Ningbo and Hangzhou, acted as Hang-Jia-Hu circuit intendant, and concurrently held the salt transport commissionership.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Ningbo and Hangzhou, acted as intendant of the Hang-Jia-Hu circuit, and concurrently held the salt transport commissionership.

sentences.zh: 六年，署按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as acting provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng (1856) he served as acting provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 粵匪由江西窺浙，梓統軍駐常山防之，授金衢嚴道。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels from Jiangxi probed Zhejiang; Zi commanded troops stationed at Changshan to defend against them and was appointed to the Jin-Qu-Yan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Cantonese rebels from Jiangxi threatened Zhejiang, Mou Zi commanded troops at Changshan to block them and was appointed intendant of the Jin-Qu-Yan circuit.

sentences.zh: 八年，粵匪陷江山，犯衢州，偕總兵李定太合擊走之，再署按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Cantonese rebels took Jiangshan and attacked Quzhou; together with Brigadier-general Li Dingtai he jointly struck and drove them off, and again served as acting provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng (1858), when Cantonese rebels seized Jiangshan and attacked Quzhou, he and Brigadier-general Li Dingtai jointly routed them, and he again served as acting provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 當賊圍杭州，梓署鹽運使兼按察使，管營務處，城守事專任之。

translations.literal: When rebels besieged Hangzhou, Zi acted as salt transport commissioner concurrent with provincial judicial commissioner, managed the camp affairs office, and was solely responsible for defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels besieged Hangzhou, Mou Zi served as acting salt transport commissioner and provincial judicial commissioner, managed the camp affairs office, and bore sole responsibility for the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 臨時調集，兵不滿四千，城大，不敷守堞。

translations.literal: Troops gathered on short notice numbered fewer than four thousand; the city was large and there were not enough to man the parapets.
translations.idiomatic: Troops gathered in haste numbered fewer than four thousand; the city was vast and there were not enough men to man the walls.

sentences.zh: 人心惶懼，動輒譁譟。

translations.literal: Hearts were fearful and at every turn there was clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the populace, and clamor broke out at every turn.

sentences.zh: 或以閉城為張皇，繼又謂戰緩為退縮。

translations.literal: Some said closing the city was alarmism; then others said fighting too slowly was retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Some denounced closing the gates as alarmism; others then accused slow fighting of cowardice.

sentences.zh: 梓奔走籌守禦，兩次縋城攻賊皆失利。

translations.literal: Zi rushed about organizing defense; twice troops were lowered by rope from the walls to attack the rebels and both times they failed.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Zi rushed about organizing the defense; twice he sent men lowered by rope from the walls to attack the rebels, and both sorties failed.

sentences.zh: 城紳促戰急，而民與兵相仇。

translations.literal: City gentry urgently pressed for battle while civilians and soldiers were mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: The city's gentry urgently pressed for battle while civilians and soldiers were at odds with one another.

sentences.zh: 梓知不可為，以死自誓。

translations.literal: Zi knew nothing could be done and vowed death upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Zi knew the situation was hopeless and vowed to die in the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 守清波門雲居山，偵賊掘地道，急開內壕。

translations.literal: He defended Qingbo Gate at Yunju Hill, detected the rebels digging a tunnel, and urgently opened an inner moat.
translations.idiomatic: He defended Qingbo Gate at Yunju Hill, detected rebels digging a tunnel, and urgently ordered an inner moat dug.

sentences.zh: 未竣，地雷猝發，城圮軍潰。

translations.literal: Before it was finished a land mine suddenly exploded, the wall collapsed, and the army routed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the work was finished a mine detonated, the wall collapsed, and the garrison broke.

sentences.zh: 身被數十創，死之。

translations.literal: His body suffered dozens of wounds and he died.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered dozens of wounds and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜卹。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported condolence honors were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, posthumous honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王有齡追論梓創議株守，奪卹典。

translations.literal: Governor Wang Youling retrospectively argued that Zi had advocated passive entrenchment and stripped his condolence honors.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Youling retrospectively blamed Mou Zi for advocating passive entrenchment and stripped his posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 及杭州再复，舉人趙之謙訴於京，下巡撫左宗棠確查。

translations.literal: When Hangzhou was recovered again, the provincial graduate Zhao Zhiqian appealed in the capital and the case was referred to Governor Zuo Zongtang for thorough investigation.
translations.idiomatic: After Hangzhou was recovered, provincial graduate Zhao Zhiqian appealed in the capital, and the court ordered Governor Zuo Zongtang to investigate.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「梓居官廉幹，臨難慘烈，請還卹典。」

translations.literal: His memorial stated: "Zi in office was upright and capable; in peril he was fierce and tragic; I request restoration of his condolence honors."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo memorialized: "Mou Zi served with integrity and ability; in the crisis he met a fierce and tragic death; I ask that his posthumous honors be restored."

sentences.zh: 後巡撫李瀚章、楊昌濬屢為疏請，贈太常寺卿，祀昭忠祠，並建專祠，予騎都尉世職，諡武烈。

translations.literal: Later Governors Li Hanzhang and Yang Changjun repeatedly memorialized on his behalf; he was posthumously made Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat of Rites, worshipped at the Zhongzhong Shrine, and a dedicated shrine was built; he was granted the hereditary office of Rider Captain and given the posthumous name Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: Later Governors Li Hanzhang and Yang Changjun repeatedly memorialized on his behalf; he was posthumously made Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat of Rites, enshrined at the Shrine of Loyal Martyrs, granted a dedicated temple, awarded the hereditary office of Rider Captain, and given the posthumous name Wulie (Martial Fierceness).

sentences.zh: =徐有壬=徐有壬，字鈞卿，順天宛平人，原籍浙江烏程。

translations.literal: Xu Youren: Xu Youren, courtesy name Junqing, a native of Wanping in Shuntian, with ancestral home in Wucheng in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Youren, courtesy name Junqing, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian, with ancestral roots in Wucheng in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光九年進士，授戶部主事，洊升郎中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of the Daoguang reign (1829), was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 出為四川成綿龍道，署按察使。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as intendant of the Cheng-Mian-Long circuit in Sichuan and acted as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed intendant of the Cheng-Mian-Long circuit in Sichuan and served concurrently as acting provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 治啯匪，擒其魁，餘黨解散。

translations.literal: He suppressed the Gun bandits, captured their chief, and the remaining followers dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the Gun bandits of eastern Sichuan, captured their leader, and the remaining followers dispersed.

sentences.zh: 遷廣東鹽運使，署按察使，清遠土匪戕官，馳剿平之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to salt transport commissioner of Guangdong and acted as provincial judicial commissioner; when Qingyuan local bandits killed an official he rushed to suppress them and pacified the region.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to salt transport commissioner of Guangdong and served as acting provincial judicial commissioner; when Qingyuan bandits killed an official he rushed to suppress them and restored order.

sentences.zh: 遷四川按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to provincial judicial commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to provincial judicial commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，下詔求言，司道率引嫌，罕所陳奏。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor ascended the throne he issued an edict seeking advice; circuit and prefect officials mostly avoided taboo and rarely memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended the throne he issued an edict seeking counsel; circuit and prefect officials mostly held back for fear of giving offense and rarely submitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 有壬獨密疏，論事切直。

translations.literal: Youren alone submitted a secret memorial, discussing affairs frankly and directly.
translations.idiomatic: Youren alone submitted a secret memorial, speaking frankly and to the point.

sentences.zh: 遷雲南布政使，調湖南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to provincial treasurer of Yunnan and then to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to provincial treasurer of Yunnan and then to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，以母憂回原籍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he returned to his native place on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianfeng (1855) he returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫何桂清奏起有壬治團防。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor He Guiqing memorialized to recall Youren to organize militia defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor He Guiqing memorialized to recall Youren from mourning to organize militia defense.

sentences.zh: 粵匪由寧國窺湖州，有壬扼長興，設伏敗之，賊去。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels from Ningguo probed Huzhou; Youren blocked them at Changxing, set an ambush and defeated them, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Cantonese rebels from Ningguo threatened Huzhou, Youren blocked them at Changxing, ambushed and defeated them, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八年，服闋，命筦江蘇糧台，擢江蘇巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his mourning ended; he was ordered to manage the Jiangsu grain bureau and was promoted to governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Xianfeng (1858), when his mourning ended, he was ordered to manage the Jiangsu grain bureau and was promoted to governor of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 槍船匪首程鵬士擾嘉興、湖州，地方官不能制，潛至蘇州，偵獲之，置諸法。

translations.literal: The musket-boat bandit chief Cheng Pengshi harassed Jiaxing and Huzhou; local officials could not control him; he secretly came to Suzhou, was detected and seized, and was executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The musket-boat bandit chief Cheng Pengshi harassed Jiaxing and Huzhou beyond the power of local officials to restrain; when he slipped into Suzhou, Youren detected and seized him and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 有壬之起，由何桂清所薦。

translations.literal: Youren's recall was due to He Guiqing's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Youren's recall from mourning was He Guiqing's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 及同官江蘇，無所阿附。

translations.literal: When they served together in Jiangsu he did not curry favor.
translations.idiomatic: When they served together in Jiangsu he did not curry favor with him.

sentences.zh: 十年春，粵匪复犯湖州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year Cantonese rebels again attacked Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year of Xianfeng (1860), Cantonese rebels again attacked Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 有壬諮商桂清，遣游擊曾秉忠率舟師往援。

translations.literal: Youren consulted with Guiqing and dispatched the raiding officer Zeng Bingzhong to lead naval forces to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Youren consulted He Guiqing and dispatched Raider Zeng Bingzhong with a naval force to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 水陸夾擊，賊被創退。

translations.literal: Land and water forces pincered the attack; the rebels were wounded and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Land and naval forces attacked in concert; the rebels were wounded and driven back.

sentences.zh: 尋復出東壩、溧陽，間道徑趨杭州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they emerged from Dongba and Liyang and by a by-path drove straight toward Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they emerged from Dongba and Liyang and by a back route drove straight toward Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 急請調提督張玉良馳援，杭州甫陷旋复。

translations.literal: He urgently requested the transfer of Provincial Commander Zhang Yuliang to rush to relieve it; Hangzhou had just fallen and was quickly recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently requested Provincial Commander Zhang Yuliang for relief; Hangzhou had just fallen and was quickly recovered.

sentences.zh: 桂清奏捷，惟言籓司王有齡功，得擾擢，有壬僅予議敘。

translations.literal: Guiqing memorialized the victory mentioning only Provincial Treasurer Wang Youling's merit; he received promotion while Youren was merely given routine commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing memorialized the victory crediting only Provincial Treasurer Wang Youling, who was promoted; Youren received only routine commendation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，和春等師潰，退守丹陽，有壬急運糧械濟之，而張國樑、和春先後戰歿，何桂清棄常州不守。

translations.literal: Before long the armies of Hechun and others were routed and retreated to defend Danyang; Youren urgently transported grain and arms to supply them, but Zhang Guoliang and Hechun successively died in battle and He Guiqing abandoned Changzhou undefended.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the armies under Hechun were routed and fell back on Danyang; Youren urgently shipped grain and arms to sustain them, but Zhang Guoliang and Hechun were killed in succession and He Guiqing abandoned Changzhou without a fight.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊遂長驅犯蘇州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the rebels then drove straight to attack Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the rebels drove straight against Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 有壬移檄責讓，桂清抗疏劾之。

translations.literal: Youren issued a dispatch reproaching him; Guiqing countered with a memorial impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Youren issued a dispatch rebuking him; Guiqing responded with a counter-memorial impeaching Youren.

sentences.zh: 張玉良自請助守城，令屯葑門外，忽夜遁。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang volunteered to assist in defending the city and was ordered to encamp outside Feng Gate, but suddenly fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang volunteered to help defend the city and was ordered to encamp outside Feng Gate, but fled suddenly in the night.

sentences.zh: 明日，有壬巡城，廣勇通賊，開門納賊。

translations.literal: The next day Youren inspected the walls; local braves colluded with the rebels and opened the gates to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, as Youren was inspecting the walls, local militia colluded with the rebels and opened the gates to admit them.

sentences.zh: 短兵巷戰，賊矛刺有壬冠，抗聲{罒馬}賊，遇害。

translations.literal: In close combat in the lanes a rebel spear pierced Youren's hat; he raised his voice and loudly reviled the rebels, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting at close quarters in the streets, a rebel spear pierced his hat; he shouted abuse at the rebels and was killed.

sentences.zh: 子震翼與妾、女同死。

translations.literal: His son Zhenyi died together with his concubine and daughter.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhenyi perished together with his concubine and daughter.

sentences.zh: 詔優恤，予騎都尉世職，諡莊愍，蘇州建專祠。

translations.literal: An edict granted exceptional posthumous care, gave a hereditary Captain of Cavalry post, posthumous name Zhuangmin, and built a dedicated shrine in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him exceptional posthumous honors, a hereditary Captain of Cavalry commission, the posthumous name Zhuangmin, and a dedicated shrine in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 有壬幼時嘗覽族譜，得遠祖應鑣闔門殉節事，慨然曰：「吾他日當如此！」

translations.literal: When young Youren once read the clan genealogy and learned how his distant ancestor Yingbiao and his whole household died for loyalty; he said with emotion: "I shall one day be like this!"
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Youren once read the clan genealogy and learned how his distant ancestor Yingbiao and his entire household had died in loyalty to the throne. Moved, he declared: "One day I too shall be like that!"

sentences.zh: 至是果驗。

translations.literal: At this it indeed came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: And so it came to pass.

sentences.zh: 八歲解勾股術，父死，依叔父於京師，師事姚學塽。

translations.literal: At eight he understood right-triangle mathematics; after his father died he relied on his uncle in the capital and took as teacher Yao Xueheng.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he mastered right-triangle mathematics; after his father's death he lived with his uncle in the capital and studied under Yao Xueheng.

sentences.zh: 學必求有用，尤精曆算，著有務民義齋算學行世。

translations.literal: In study he always sought what was useful; he was especially skilled in calendar calculation and authored Wumin Yizhai Suanxue, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued only useful learning, excelled above all at calendrical calculation, and published Wumin Yizhai Suanxue.

sentences.zh: =王有齡=王有齡，字雪軒，福建侯官人。

translations.literal: Wang Youling: Wang Youling, courtesy name Xuexuan, a native of Houguan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youling, courtesy name Xuexuan, was a native of Houguan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 道光中，捐納浙江鹽大使，改知縣。

translations.literal: During the Daoguang reign he bought appointment as Zhejiang salt commissioner and was transferred to county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign he purchased an appointment as Zhejiang salt commissioner and later entered service as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 歷慈谿、定海、鄞、仁和，皆有聲。

translations.literal: He served in Cixi, Dinghai, Yin, and Renhe, all with renown.
translations.idiomatic: His stints as magistrate in Cixi, Dinghai, Yin, and Renhe all won him a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 以勞晉秩知府。

translations.literal: For his labors he was promoted in rank to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect in recognition of his service.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，授杭州知府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng he was appointed Hangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Xianfeng reign he was appointed prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫何桂清器其幹略，迭署鹽運使、按察使，擢雲南糧儲道，仍留浙治防。

translations.literal: Governor He Guiqing valued his capacity and resourcefulness; he served successively as acting salt transport commissioner and provincial judicial commissioner, was promoted to Yunnan grain superintendent, yet remained in Zhejiang to manage defense.
translations.idiomatic: Governor He Guiqing admired his executive ability and repeatedly entrusted him as acting salt transport commissioner and provincial judicial commissioner; though promoted to Yunnan grain superintendent, he was kept in Zhejiang to manage defense.

sentences.zh: 桂清總督兩江，奏調赴上海議通商稅則。

translations.literal: When Guiqing became governor-general of the Two Jiangs he memorialized to transfer him to Shanghai to discuss commercial treaty tariffs.
translations.idiomatic: After Guiqing became governor-general of the Two Jiangs, he memorialized to send Youling to Shanghai to negotiate commercial treaty tariffs.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢江蘇按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Jiangsu provincial judicial commissioner and transferred to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Jiangsu judicial commissioner and then provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 有齡長於理財，桂清素信之深，一切倚畀，益得發舒，事皆專斷，巡撫受成而已。

translations.literal: Youling was skilled at financial management; Guiqing had long trusted him deeply and relied on him for everything, so he was increasingly able to give full play to his talents; he decided all matters on his own, and the governor merely accepted completed work.
translations.idiomatic: Youling excelled at financial management; Guiqing had long placed deep trust in him and delegated everything. Youling grew ever bolder in exercising authority, deciding matters on his own while the governor merely signed off on the results.

sentences.zh: 十年，粵匪陷杭州，將以掣動江南全，局故援兵至，賊即不戰而走。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Cantonese rebels captured Hangzhou, intending thereby to tie up the whole Jiangnan situation; but when relief troops arrived the rebels withdrew without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Cantonese rebels took Hangzhou to pin down the whole Jiangnan front, relief troops arrived and the rebels withdrew without a fight.

sentences.zh: 桂清推功於有齡，遂擢浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: Guiqing attributed the credit to Youling, who was then promoted to Zhejiang governor.
translations.idiomatic: Guiqing credited Youling with the success, and Youling was promoted to governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 詔趣率兵速赴，會辦軍務及善後事宜，而賊已回撲江南大營。

translations.literal: An edict urged him to lead troops quickly to the scene to jointly manage military affairs and post-disaster measures, but the rebels had already turned back to assault the Jiangnan Grand Camp.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to hurry with troops to jointly handle military affairs and recovery, but the rebels had already swung back against the Jiangnan Grand Camp.

sentences.zh: 和春等軍潰，常州、蘇州相繼陷，進逼嘉興，提督張玉良迎擊，敗績，杭州戒嚴。

translations.literal: The armies of Hechun and others were routed; Changzhou and Suzhou fell in succession; pressing toward Jiaxing, Regional Commander Zhang Yuliang met them in battle and was defeated; Hangzhou went on alert.
translations.idiomatic: The armies under Hechun collapsed; Changzhou and Suzhou fell in turn; as the rebels pressed toward Jiaxing, Regional Commander Zhang Yuliang gave battle and was beaten. Hangzhou went on high alert.

sentences.zh: 有齡率閩兵屯北新關外，遣撫標兵要賊於賣魚橋，夾擊敗之，賊乃卻。

translations.literal: Youling led Fujian troops to encamp outside Beixin Pass, sent provincial garrison troops to intercept the rebels at Maiyu Bridge, defeated them in pincer attack, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Youling led Fujian troops to encamp outside Beixin Pass, sent provincial garrison troops to block the rebels at Maiyu Bridge, and defeated them in a pincer; the rebels fell back.

sentences.zh: 設捐輸局，奏請派在籍前左副都御史王履謙、前漕運總督邵燦督同辦理。

translations.literal: He established a donation bureau and memorialized to assign former Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Lüqian and former Grain Transport Director Shao Can, both on leave in their native places, to supervise it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a donation bureau and memorialized to appoint former Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Lüqian and former Grain Transport Director Shao Can, both resident in their home districts, to supervise collections jointly.

sentences.zh: 賊眾十餘萬由徽州入浙，陷嚴州，合嘉興、廣德兩路分撲省城，有齡偕將軍瑞昌調兵迎擊走之，圍得解，复餘杭，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand rebels entered Zhejiang from Huizhou, captured Yanzhou, and combined forces from Jiaxing and Guangde to assault the provincial capital in two columns; Youling with General Ruichang mobilized troops to meet and drive them off, the siege was lifted, Yuhang was recovered, and he was given the first-grade official's button.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand rebels entered Zhejiang from Huizhou, took Yanzhou, and converged on the provincial capital from Jiaxing and Guangde; Youling and General Ruichang rallied troops, drove them off, lifted the siege, recovered Yuhang, and earned the first-grade official's button.

sentences.zh: 尋复嚴州。

translations.literal: Soon Yanzhou was recovered too.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was recovered shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 十一年，复江山、常山、富陽、遂安、海寧、臨安等縣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Jiangshan, Changshan, Fuyang, Suian, Haining, Lin'an, and other counties were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he recovered Jiangshan, Changshan, Fuyang, Suian, Haining, Lin'an, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 賊擾​​太湖東山，總兵王之敬戰失利。

translations.literal: Rebels harassed Dongshan on Lake Tai; Regional Commander Wang Zhijing was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels raided Dongshan on Lake Tai and Regional Commander Wang Zhijing was beaten in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 至夏，賊复陷江山、常山、長興、金華、遂昌、松陽、處州、永康、義烏，革職留任。

translations.literal: By summer the rebels again captured Jiangshan, Changshan, Changxing, Jinhua, Suichang, Songyang, Chuzhou, Yongkang, and Yiwu; he was stripped of office but retained in post.
translations.idiomatic: By summer the rebels had retaken Jiangshan, Changshan, Changxing, Jinhua, Suichang, Songyang, Chuzhou, Yongkang, and Yiwu; Youling was dismissed from office but kept on duty.

sentences.zh: 張玉良扼要隘為諸軍應援，兵先潰，賊勢益橫。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang held key passes to support the other armies, but his troops collapsed first and rebel power grew more rampant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang held key passes to support the other armies, but his men broke first and rebel strength grew unchecked.

sentences.zh: 檄諸將往援，無應者，處州鎮總兵文瑞率江西援兵三千，有齡待之素厚，乃自請行。

translations.literal: He issued orders to the generals to go to the rescue, but none responded; Chuzhou garrison commander Wen Rui led three thousand Jiangxi relief troops; Youling had long treated him well, so he volunteered to go himself.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the generals to reinforce the front, but none answered; Chuzhou garrison commander Wen Rui had three thousand Jiangxi relief troops—Youling had always treated him generously and now volunteered to go in person.

sentences.zh: 進駐金華孝順街，聞蘭谿兵敗，遽潰；

translations.literal: He advanced to encamp at Xiaoshun Street in Jinhua; on hearing that troops at Lanxi had been defeated he suddenly collapsed in rout;
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Xiaoshun Street in Jinhua, but on news of defeat at Lanxi his men suddenly broke and fled;

sentences.zh: 退守浦江，賊躡之，檄師往援，半途复潰：浦江、嚴州相繼陷。

translations.literal: He retreated to defend Pujiang; the rebels pursued; he ordered troops to the rescue but they again collapsed halfway: Pujiang and Yanzhou fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to hold Pujiang, but the rebels pressed close; relief troops routed again halfway—and Pujiang and Yanzhou fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 總兵劉季三、副將劉芳戰死於富陽。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Liu Jisan and Vice Commander Liu Fang died in battle at Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Liu Jisan and Vice Commander Liu Fang were killed fighting at Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 諸將見賊多走，不任戰，惟要索軍食。

translations.literal: The generals, seeing rebels in great numbers, fled rather than fight and only demanded army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, outnumbered, fled rather than stand and fight, demanding only rations.

sentences.zh: 富民捐輸已倦，而有司持之急。

translations.literal: Wealthy people had grown weary of donating, yet officials pressed them urgently.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy had grown weary of giving, yet officials pressed them all the harder.

sentences.zh: 於是團練大臣王履謙劾有齡虐捐，遇事多齟《齒吾》，上疏互訐。

translations.literal: Thereupon militia commissioner Wang Lüqian impeached Youling for cruel levies of donations; on affairs they often had mutual conflict and memorialized to accuse each other.
translations.idiomatic: Militia Commissioner Wang Lüqian then impeached Youling for brutal donation drives; on nearly every issue they clashed, trading memorials accusing each other.

sentences.zh: 十月，蕭山、諸暨及紹興府皆陷，餉源遂絕。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Xiaoshan, Zhuji, and Shaoxing prefecture all fell; sources of pay were thus cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Xiaoshan, Zhuji, and Shaoxing prefecture all fell, and the province's supply lines were severed.

sentences.zh: 時援軍多不足恃，有齡復奏用李元度為按察使，募湘勇八千入浙，至龍遊，阻不得前。

translations.literal: At the time most relief armies were unreliable; Youling again memorialized to employ Li Yuandu as provincial judicial commissioner, raised eight thousand Hunan braves to enter Zhejiang; they reached Longyou but were blocked and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Most relief armies could not be relied upon; Youling again memorialized to appoint Li Yuandu judicial commissioner and raise eight thousand Hunan braves for Zhejiang, but they reached Longyou and could go no farther.

sentences.zh: 賊酋李秀成悉眾圍杭州城，副將楊金榜敗死，張玉良攻克羅木營賊壘，亦中飛砲死：城中奪氣，且食盡，饑民死者枕藉。

translations.literal: Rebel chief Li Xiucheng mustered all his forces to besiege Hangzhou; Vice Commander Yang Jinbang was defeated and killed; Zhang Yuliang stormed the rebel stronghold at Luomuying but also died from a stray cannon shot: morale in the city collapsed, and food was exhausted; starved civilians died in heaps.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Li Xiucheng threw his whole army against Hangzhou; Vice Commander Yang Jinbang was beaten and killed; Zhang Yuliang took the rebel stronghold at Luomuying but was killed by a chance shell—and inside the city morale collapsed, provisions ran out, and the starving dead lay piled in the streets.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊梯城入，兵潰，有齡服毒不死，縊於閣，秀成見之，為具棺殮焉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the rebels scaled the walls to enter; the troops collapsed; Youling took poison but did not die and hanged himself in a pavilion; Xiucheng saw him and had a coffin prepared for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month rebels scaled the walls; the garrison broke; Youling swallowed poison without dying and hanged himself in a pavilion. Xiucheng had him coffined and buried with honor.

sentences.zh: 事聞，言官顏宗儀、高延祜、硃潮先後疏劾勒捐斂怨，下曾國籓按，奏言：「有齡在浙，官紳不和，不能馭兵，以致僨事；

translations.literal: When word reached the throne, censor Yan Zongyi, Gao Yanhu, and Zhu Chao successively memorialized impeaching him for forced donations arousing resentment; the case was referred to Zeng Guofan for investigation, who memorialized: "Youling in Zhejiang—officials and gentry were at odds, he could not control the troops, and matters failed thereby;
translations.idiomatic: When the news reached court, censors Yan Zongyi, Gao Yanhu, and Zhu Chao memorialized in succession denouncing his coercive fund-raising; the case was referred to Zeng Guofan, who reported: "In Zhejiang Youling could not harmonize officials and gentry or command the army, and affairs failed for it;

sentences.zh: 仍以糧盡援絕，見危授命，大節無虧。」

translations.literal: yet with grain exhausted and relief cut off, facing peril he gave his life—the great integrity was not compromised.
translations.idiomatic: yet with grain gone and relief cut off he faced death unflinching—his ultimate loyalty was beyond reproach.

sentences.zh: 詔依例賜卹，諡壯愍。

translations.literal: An edict granted posthumous compensation according to regulation and posthumous name Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted posthumous compensation by statute and the posthumous name Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 入祀昭忠祠，浙江，福建建專祠。

translations.literal: He was entered in the Shrine of Loyalty; dedicated shrines were built in Zhejiang and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the Shrine of Loyal Faithful Service, with dedicated temples built in Zhejiang and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 同殉者，學政張錫庚、提督饒廷選、總兵文瑞、署布政使麟趾、按察使甯曾綸、督糧道暹福、仁和知縣吳保豐。

translations.literal: Those who died with him: Education Commissioner Zhang Xigeng, Regional Commander Rao Tingxuan, Regional Commander Wen Rui, Acting Provincial Treasurer Linzhi, Judicial Commissioner Ning Zenglun, Grain Superintendent Xianfu, Renhe Magistrate Wu Baofeng.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died with him included Education Commissioner Zhang Xigeng, Regional Commander Rao Tingxuan, Regional Commander Wen Rui, Acting Provincial Treasurer Linzhi, Judicial Commissioner Ning Zenglun, Grain Superintendent Xianfu, and Renhe Magistrate Wu Baofeng.

sentences.zh: 錫庚、廷選、文瑞並自有傳。

translations.literal: Xigeng, Tingxuan, and Wen Rui each have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Xigeng, Tingxuan, and Wen Rui each have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：粵匪自陷岳州，勢不可遏。

translations.literal: Commentary: The commentary says: From the time the Cantonese rebels captured Yuezhou their momentum could not be checked.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Once the Cantonese rebels took Yuezhou, their momentum could no longer be checked.

sentences.zh: 及犯武昌，援兵雖至，無能為力。

translations.literal: When they attacked Wuchang, though relief troops arrived they could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When they struck Wuchang, relief armies arrived but could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 安慶倉猝籌防，益無措手矣。

translations.literal: Anqing rushed to plan defense, and there was even less room to maneuver.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing was scrambling to prepare defenses, and even that was beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 武昌凡三陷，湖北兵不可用，曾國籓言之痛切。

translations.literal: Wuchang fell three times in all; Hubei troops were unusable—Zeng Guofan spoke of this with bitter pain.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang fell three times; Hubei troops were useless—Zeng Guofan wrote of it with bitter anguish.

sentences.zh: 杭州初陷，由於無兵，後則蘇、常已失，脣亡齒寒。

translations.literal: Hangzhou's first fall was due to having no troops; later Suzhou and Changzhou were already lost—the lips gone, the teeth grow cold.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou fell the first time for lack of troops; later, after Suzhou and Changzhou were lost, the teeth felt the cold when the lips were gone.

sentences.zh: 蘇州素倚江南大軍為屏蔽，大軍潰，則勢難幸全。

translations.literal: Suzhou had always relied on the Jiangnan Grand Army as its shield; when the Grand Army collapsed, it was hard to hope for survival.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou had always relied on the Jiangnan Grand Army as its shield; once that army collapsed, survival was unlikely.

sentences.zh: 常大淳、蔣文慶、陶恩培、羅遵殿、徐有壬諸人，皆不失為承平良吏，短於應變，或因受事於已危，莫能挽救。

translations.literal: Chang Dachun, Jiang Wenqing, Tao Enpei, Luo Zundian, Xu Youren and the like were none the less good officials in peace, short in adapting to change, or because they took office when danger was already present, unable to rescue matters.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Dachun, Jiang Wenqing, Tao Enpei, Luo Zundian, Xu Youren, and their like were all capable peace-time administrators, ill suited to crisis—or charged with cities already beyond saving.

sentences.zh: 王有齡素負才略，以掊克失人心，措施亦未盡當焉。

translations.literal: Wang Youling had long possessed talent and strategy, but through exactions lost popular support; his measures also were not entirely appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Youling was a man of real talent, but exactions cost him the people's hearts, and his policies were not always sound.

sentences.zh: 吉爾杭阿治兵有法，克上海為全功，朝廷倚以規复鎮江，使非中道而殞，必有成效，其建樹非諸人所可同語也。

translations.literal: Ji Erhanga governed troops with method; capturing Shanghai was his complete achievement; the court relied on him to plan recovery of Zhenjiang—if he had not died midway he would surely have achieved results; his accomplishments are not comparable with those of the others.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Erhanga drilled his troops with discipline; his capture of Shanghai was a complete victory, and the court looked to him to recover Zhenjiang. Had he not died mid-campaign, he would surely have achieved much—accomplishments none of the others could equal.
